text:
Things that die never rise again,

things that die never return again.

The vessels break and the glass that remains

is dust forever and forever will be!


When the buds fall from the branch

they will never bloom a second time…

The flowers broken by the impious wind

are spent forever, forevermore!


The days that were, the lost days,

the inert days will not return!

How sad the hours that slipped away

beneath solitude's beating wing!


How sad the shadows, the baleful shadows,

the shadows made by our wickedness!

O things gone, things withered,

the celestial things that leave us so!


Heart… be still!… Cover yourself with sores!…

—with infected sores—cover yourself with evil!…

Let everyone who comes die upon touching you,

cursed heart that vexes my longing!


Farewell forever, all my sweetnesses!

Farewell, my joy full of goodness!

O dead things, withered things,

the celestial things that never return!…

translation.title: Things That Die Never Rise Again...
translation.editorial_note: The translation retains the insistent repetitions, exclamations, and direct address that make the poem a chant of irreversible loss.
